facts.fact: NIDA's director general says the new digital ID system is integrated with Rwanda's civil registration and vital statistics system, without saying which records pass.

systems.tiers: number, digital token, card with QR code

facts.fact: NIDA has registered 2,373,854 people for the new digital ID out of an estimated 14 million, about 16% of the 14.6 million population (divided by the population held, not stated in the document), at about 40,000 a day.

systems.tiers: number, digital token, card with QR code

RWA.note: Newborn registration is mentioned only as a future activity of sector offices; no number at birth is stated.
The document does not say who operates or maintains the platform.
No public register keyed on the ID number is stated.

facts.fact: NIDA is registering citizens for the new biometric digital ID (fingerprints, face and iris) under the Single Digital Identification Law, building on identity cards issued since 1962; all current cards become invalid by June 2027.
